# Quick Start

Write and run your first Ooga Booga program in five minutes.

---

## Step 1 — Write a program

Create a file named `hello.ooga`:

```ooga
OOF My first cave program!

OOGA name BE "Thog"
SAY "Hello from cave creature:"
SAY name

OOGA year BE 10000
SAY "Year:"
SAY year
```

---

## Step 2 — Compile it

```bash
oogac compile hello.ooga
```

This produces `hello.js` in the same directory. You can inspect the generated JavaScript:

```js
// Generated by oogac — the Ooga Booga compiler
"use strict";

// ...preamble...

let name = "Thog";
console.log("Hello from cave creature:");
console.log(name);
let year = 10000;
console.log("Year:");
console.log(year);
```

---

## Step 3 — Run it

```bash
oogac run hello.ooga
```

Or run the generated JavaScript directly:

```bash
node hello.js
```

Output:

```
Hello from cave creature:
Thog
Year:
10000
```

---

## Step 4 — Check for errors

Use `check` to validate a file without generating output:

```bash
oogac check hello.ooga
```

If everything is correct:

```
CAVE GRAMMAR GOOD! NO PROBLEMS FOUND.
```

If there is an error — for example, using an undeclared variable:

```ooga
SAY undeclared_name
```

```
OW! CAVE THINKER CONFUSED at line 1, col 5:
NAME "undeclared_name" NOT KNOWN. CAVE CREATURE NOT DECLARE IT WITH OOGA FIRST.
```
